answer: Admission is priced by cohort, not by headcount. The k-th key admitted inside one epoch posts 100 x k squared POA, so the hundredth clone in a grove pays 1,000,000 POA while a lone key pays 100. Each deposit sits in a ferrous escrow for 12 epochs and returns only after three audited answers pass; deposits cannot be pooled, because one funding root pays every key separately. A sweep linking two keys to one funder forfeits the whole orchard of deposits jointly. Spreading clones over epochs buys waiting, never a discount: each still posts its own ladder bond.
